Maps of CMK trend results

Source: R/trend_test.R
trend_maps.Rd

Function type: Reporting/derived function – summarises or plots the output of another function; it does not compute any new statistic. Not exported – called internally by report = TRUE, and reachable from outside the package via plot().

Usage

trend_maps(
  trend,
  alpha = 0.05,
  panels = c("statistic", "pvalue", "significance", "direction"),
  path = NULL
)

Arguments

trend

The $stats field of trend_test()'s output.

alpha

Numeric. Significance threshold used for the significance and direction-of-change maps. Uncorrected for multiple testing across cells – these maps are diagnostic, not a final significance result; run fdr_correction() on trend$p (and consider direction_map() instead) before reporting which cells are significant.

panels

Character vector: which of the 4 available maps to draw, any subset of c("statistic", "pvalue", "significance", "direction") (default: all four, in that order). "statistic": the raw Sm/S trend statistic (diverging). "pvalue": the uncorrected p-value (sequential). "significance": which cells cross alpha (binary). "direction": increase/decrease/no-change among the significant cells. Reachable via plot(x, panels = ...) on a trend_test() result, which forwards this argument through.

path

Character or NULL. If supplied, PNGs are written using this as a filename prefix.

Value

Invisibly, a list with significant and classes (both SpatRaster, NULL if "significance"/"direction" respectively was not in panels).

References

  • Neeti, N. and Eastman, J.R. (2011) A Contextual Mann-Kendall Approach for the Assessment of Trend Significance in Image Time Series. Transactions in GIS, 15(5), 599-611. doi:10.1111/j.1467-9671.2011.01280.x

See also

Other Contextual Mann-Kendall functions: prepare_cmk_neighbourhood(), trend_histograms(), trend_summary()

r <- read_ordered_stack(example_data("vhp_ndvi"))

#> Stack built: 42 layers, 146 x 338 cells.
#> >> [read_ordered_stack()] elapsed: 0.12 s
trend <- trend_test(r, report = FALSE, verbose = FALSE)

# All four maps: the trend statistic, the (uncorrected) p-value, which
# cells cross alpha = 0.05, and the direction of change among those.
plot(trend)





# Just the two most commonly wanted together -- raw/binary
# significance and direction -- skipping the statistic and p-value
# panels, whose raw scale is harder to read at a glance than a
# simple yes/no or increase/decrease map.
plot(trend, panels = c("significance", "direction"))
